newsitem.title: INDIA: India sugar pushed up by shortage of stock.
newsitem.headline: India sugar pushed up by shortage of stock.

text.p: Sugar prices lifted further on the local market on Monday, dealers said.

Absence of fresh arrivals and shortage of ready stock pushed prices upward though buying was moderate. Transport operators in western India have gone on strike from Sunday midnight to protest against a new tax and a hike in insurance premiums.
"Arrivals of sugar from mills to the Bombay market has halted due to the strike," one dealer said. "Transport operators across the country will stop work from midnight onwards."
In ready delivery sugar S-30 rose 10 rupees at 1,300/1,360 rupees per quintal while M-30 rose 20 rupees at 1,350/1,450.
"Last week retail consumers had bought more sugar than expected ahead of the strike and today demand remained moderate at the higher level," one broker said.
"Prices in the ready delivery may extend gains if the strike of the transport operators is prolonged," he added.

Sugar mill delivery remained unquoted as millers have sold most of the free sale sugar out of the quota for March. Free sale quota for April is 700,000 tonnes and traders were awaiting the state-wise allocation of this quota by the union government. Free sale quota for March was also 700,000 tonnes.
